title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is buzzing with activity as geopolitical tensions simmer and companies scramble for funding. From GPS jamming efforts to the latest SPAC deals, the landscape is anything but dull.

themes.title: GPS Jamming Escalates
themes.body: Russia's renewed efforts to jam GPS signals are raising eyebrows and concerns among defense analysts. This move could complicate operations for both military and civilian users in affected regions.

themes.title: SPACs and IPOs Resurface
themes.body: Quantum Space's impending SPAC deal highlights a potential thaw in the defense-tech IPO market. Meanwhile, Palantir's extension on the TITAN program suggests that government contracts remain a reliable revenue stream.

themes.title: U.S.-China Space Competition
themes.body: The upcoming WRC-27 conference is set to be a battleground for U.S.-China rivalry in space. Expect discussions on satellite frequencies to turn into a proxy for broader geopolitical tensions.

themes.title: Innovations in Spacesuits
themes.body: Axiom and Prada's collaboration on spacesuit design is a curious blend of fashion and function. While it may raise eyebrows, it underscores the increasing importance of aesthetics in the space industry.
